CHAPTER I
Preliminary
1. Short title, extent, commencement and application.‑‑‑(1)
This Ordinance may be called the (Subs. for West Pakistan by P.O. 4 of 1975, s. 2 (1) &
Sch. Gaz. of Pak. Extr. Pt. 2, 1 Aug. 1975, p. 435.)[Provincial] Employees' official Security Ordinance, 1965.
(2) It extends to the whole of (Subs. for
West Pakistan, except the Tribunal Areas, ibid.) [Pakistan] (Ordinance applied to the Tribal areas of Baluchistan by
Regulation III of 1974 (29 July 1974). Baluchistan Gaz. Extr. 29 July 1974.)
(3) It shall come into force at
once but shall apply only to such areas, classes of persons, industries or
establishments, from such date or dates and with regard to the provision of
such benefits as Government molt, by notification (Ordinance applied in Baluchistan to
specified establishments. Baluchistan Gaz. No. Extr., Jan. 5. 1989.)specify in this behalf.
[Notes.‑The scheme of the
Ordinance is that, it comes into force at once and extends to the whole of West
Pakistan, it does not apply is to any areas, classes of persons, industries or
establishments. This is to be done by a separate notification from such date as
may be specified and also in respect of such benefits as may be fixed in the
notification. The idea is gradual application anal extension of Ordinance as
regards areas, industries and benefits depending upon experience gained and the
progress made in enforcement.
Ordinance does not apply to all
concerns owned lay a particular person or legal entity but applies only to an
industry or establishment specifically stated in the notification. Where two
shops A and B were owned by the same owner and goods manufactured at B were
sold at A and notification was issued for shop A only, hold that these facts
alone did not connect the two sufficiently for purpose of making the ordinance
applicable to industry B as well. [1975 LLC 69=PLD 1915 Kar. 36 (H.C. Kar.):
Kashmir Corner vs. Sind Employees' Social Security Institution Karachi].
There is no restriction on the by
Government to apply the Ordinance by notification or some of its provisions to
an industry or establishment irrespective of the number of employees. The word
"classes" does not qualify the words "industries " of
"establishments". The ordinance can be applied to particular
industries or establishments. In case of change of ownership, the Ordinance
continues to apply. When such a notification has been issued, a Social Security
Court under section 61 has no jurisdiction. to adjudicate and decide upon the
constitutional question of vires of the notification issued under S. 1 (3).
Statutory Tribunals of Limited jurisdiction have to function strictly within
the sphere allotted to them under the Statute.
Once an establishment is notified
under S. 1 (3) the benefits under the Ordinance would accrue to all employees
working in the establish ment or in connection with the work of the same. The
!utter categories of employees tray not be physically located at the notified
address but in that case an inquiry would be necessary to establish whether
they are in fact working in connection with the wont of the notified establish ment,
Government reserves its right
under S. I (3) to include any areas or classes of industries of establishments.
No restriction on Govern ment to apply the Ordinance, or some provisions thereof,
to plaintiff's firm, irrespective of number of its employees and i

4. Management.‑(1) The general direction and superintend of
the affairs of the Institution shall vest in a Governing Body which, with the
assistance of a Commissioner, may exercise all powers and do all acts and
things which may be exercised or done by the Institution.
(2) In discharging its functions,
the Institution shall be guided lay such instructions on questions of policy as
may be given to it from time to time by Government, which shall be the sole
judge as to whether any instructions are on a question of policy or not.
[Notes.‑‑ It is
obligatory on the institution to follow the instructions the Government on
questions of policy. Moreover Government is the sole judge as to whether any
instructions are on a question of policy or not. Thus the Government reserves
to itself unfettered discretion.]

9. Supersession of the Governing Body.‑‑(1) If, in the
opinion of Government, the Governing Body has persistently failed to perform
the duties imposed upon it by or under this Ordinance or has abused its powers,
Government may, by notification, supersede the Governing Body:
Provided that before such
supersession, Government shall give the Governing Body a reasonable opportunity
to show cause why it should not be superseded, and shall consider any
explanation or objection which it submits.
(2) Upon the publication of a
notification under sub‑section (1), the persons holding office as
Chairman, and Members shall cease to hold such office.
(3) Immediately upon the supersession of a Governing Body.
Government shall constitute another Governing Body by appointing new Members in
accordance with the provisions of section 5.( The word "the" subs. by
"an" in its application to Punjab by Punjab Ord. X of 1971. s. 3.)

opinion of the Government which is a subjective matter is the sole deciding

CHAPTER V
Benefits
38‑A Medical care of
dependents, etc.--- (New section 38‑A
inserted by the Labour Laws (Amendment) Ord 1993 (XXIII of 1993) No.F'.2(1)/93
Pub. the 25th Scpt. 1993 s.4 (5))
When a secured person dies other than due to any employment injury, his
dependents shall, subject to regulations, be entitled to medical care for one
year from the date of death of the secured person:
Provided that the deceased
secured person had been in continuous employment of an establishment for not
less than twelve months immediately preceding his death;
Provided further that where the
deceased secured person was a seasonal employee, his dependent, shall be
entitled to medical care for six months from the date of death of such secured
person:
Provided also that the deceased
has been in. employment of an establishment for not less than six months during
two continuous seasons immediately .preceding his death.]
[Notes.‑ Pre‑natal
and post‑natal care is only admissible to a secured woman in during the
six calendar months immediately preceding, contributions are paid for not less
than 90 days.]
